notes: Step 1 parts were correct and are unchanged: 9 parts, with 5 jumper wires as in the circuit image.

The image's breadboard is drawn with rows f-j in the top half and a-e in the bottom half. The catalogue calls rows a-e bank 't' and rows f-j bank 'b', so the lower half of the image is bank 't' and the rails beside it are tp/tn.

Button legs sit in columns 4 and 6 and straddle the centre gap. Side 1 (1.l/1.r) is column 4 and side 2 (2.l/2.r) is column 6. Each side's two legs are joined inside the button, as in a real tactile switch.
Column 4 is wired by the orange wire to the + rail, which is fed from 5V by the red wire. So the button's other leg goes to 5V.

Column 6 holds the teal wire from digital pin 2 (at 6b.i) and the 10K pull-down resistor (6t.c to 9t.c). The short black wire (9t.b) takes the resistor's far end to the - rail, which the black wire connects to Uno GND.
Rail hole numbers (tp.1, tn.1, tp.4, tn.8) are approximate. Only the rail each wire lands on matters, because each rail is one strip.
The resistor is read as spanning columns 6 to 9. Its right end lines up with the short black wire's column.
The built-in LED on pin 13 is part of the Uno, so no external LED is used.
